# Alert engine evaluation (generated by `python -m scripts.evaluate_alerts`)

Synthetic data, seed 42, 150 patients, 182 days. Engine replayed daily from day 112. Rules version rules-0.1.0. Numbers are measured, not edited.

## seizure_increase on `rising` patients

| metric | value |
|---|---|
| injected cases | 29 |
| flagged after onset (sensitivity) | 28/29 = 0.966 |
| median days from onset to first flag | 12.0 |
| range of days to flag | 0–51 |
| stable patients wrongly flagged (false alarm rate) | 33/80 = 0.412 |

Not flagged: P-D641AE (onset day(s) 122).

## adherence_drop on `poor_adherence` patients

| metric | value |
|---|---|
| injected cases | 18 |
| flagged after onset (sensitivity) | 18/18 = 1.000 |
| median days from onset to first flag | 5.5 |
| range of days to flag | 2–10 |
| stable patients wrongly flagged (false alarm rate) | 13/80 = 0.163 |

## Trend threshold trade-off (exploration on the same data — for the neurologist to decide)

| min_ratio | min_recent_count | sensitivity (rising) | median days to flag | false alarm rate (stable) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2.0 (config default) | 3 | 28/29 | 12.0 | 33/80 |
| 2.0 | 4 | 27/29 | 13 | 28/80 |
| 3.0 | 3 | 18/29 | 17.0 | 12/80 |
| 3.0 | 4 | 17/29 | 17 | 9/80 |

Note: some rising/poor-adherence onsets fall before day 112; for those, detection is counted from day 112 and the delay is still measured from the true onset, so their delays are longer.
